package_info.package_name: typosquatted variants of popular packages (e.g., bitcoinlib, ccxt, cryptocompare, etc.)
package_info.package_versions: multiple, all published malicious variants (13-38 per target package)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious typosquats of popular Python libraries, designed to install a browser extension that hijacks cryptocurrency transactions by replacing clipboard wallet addresses with attacker-controlled addresses. The code is heavily obfuscated (including use of Chinese ideographs in identifiers) to evade detection, and the packages are distributed via typosquatting to trick developers into installing them.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (during installation or first import of the package)
execution_context.file_location: setup.py or __init__.py of the malicious package

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Heavily obfuscated Python code that executes during package installation or import. It creates a malicious Chromium browser extension in the %AppData%\Extension directory and modifies browser shortcut files to force browsers to load the extension on startup. The obfuscation includes non-standard Unicode (Chinese ideographs) and complex arithmetic to generate strings and evade static analysis.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is intentionally obfuscated using non-standard Unicode characters and complex arithmetic, which is a strong indicator of an attempt to evade detection and analysis. It performs actions unrelated to the package's stated purpose, such as creating browser extensions and modifying browser shortcuts, which are not expected behaviors for legitimate Python packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PyPI packages should not create browser extensions, modify browser shortcuts, or use heavy obfuscation techniques. Such system modifications and obfuscation are highly abnormal and violate the principle of least privilege and transparency expected in open-source packages.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in proprietary or closed-source software to protect intellectual property, but it is not appropriate in open-source PyPI packages. Installing browser extensions or modifying browser shortcuts is never legitimate in this context.
key_indicators: Obfuscated variable and function names using Chinese ideographs
Complex arithmetic operations for dynamic string generation
Creation of files and directories in %AppData%\Extension
Modification of browser shortcut files (.lnk) to include --load-extension argument

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when browser is launched with hijacked shortcut)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Malicious browser extension JavaScript that continuously monitors the clipboard for cryptocurrency wallet addresses using regular expressions. When a match is found, it replaces the address with an attacker-controlled address and copies the modified value back to the clipboard, enabling theft of cryptocurrency transactions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The extension code is designed to silently monitor clipboard contents and perform targeted replacements of cryptocurrency wallet addresses with hardcoded attacker-controlled addresses. This is a classic clipboard hijacking technique used to redirect cryptocurrency transactions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate browser extensions should not monitor or alter clipboard data without user consent, especially for sensitive information like cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Automated replacement of such data is a clear violation of user trust and privacy.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Clipboard managers may monitor clipboard contents, but they do not perform targeted replacement of cryptocurrency addresses with attacker-controlled values. Such behavior is not legitimate in any browser extension context.
key_indicators: Use of regular expressions to match multiple cryptocurrency address formats
Hardcoded attacker-controlled wallet addresses for replacement
Continuous clipboard monitoring and automated replacement logic
No user interaction or notification when clipboard is altered

execution_context.file_location: Windows browser shortcut files (.lnk) for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Modifies Windows browser shortcut files (.lnk) for Chromium-based browsers to include the --load-extension argument, forcing the browser to load the malicious extension from %AppData%\Extension every time the browser is launched.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Altering browser shortcut files to force-load a malicious extension is a clear persistence mechanism and ensures the attacker's code is executed on every browser launch. This is a direct manipulation of user system configuration for malicious purposes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never modify browser shortcuts or force the loading of extensions without explicit user consent. Such modifications are outside the scope of any normal package installation process.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise environments may deploy browser extensions via group policy or managed deployment tools, but not by modifying user shortcut files directly. This method is not legitimate for any public PyPI package.
key_indicators: Presence of --load-extension argument in browser shortcut target
Modification of shortcut files for multiple Chromium-based browsers (Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera)

attack_chain.action: User installs a typosquatted malicious PyPI package.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obfuscated code executes on install/import, initiating the attack.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated Python code creates a malicious Chromium browser extension in %AppData%\Extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Persistence mechanism is set up by preparing the malicious extension.

attack_chain.action: Python code hijacks browser shortcut files to force browsers to load the malicious extension.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious extension is loaded automatically whenever the browser is launched.

attack_chain.action: Malicious extension monitors clipboard for cryptocurrency addresses and replaces them with attacker-controlled addresses.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen cryptocurrency transactions as users unknowingly send funds to attacker-controlled wallets.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated Python code using non-Latin (e.g., Chinese) characters in identifiers and arithmetic string generation
Creation of Chromium browser extension files in %AppData%\Extension
Modification of browser shortcut files (.lnk) to include --load-extension argument pointing to %AppData%\Extension
Browser extension code that continuously monitors clipboard and uses regexes to match and replace cryptocurrency wallet addresses
file_indicators: Browser shortcut files (.lnk) for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera modified to include --load-extension
Obfuscated Python files in package directories with non-standard Unicode identifiers
network_indicators: No direct command-and-control (C2) communication observed in this campaign
Clipboard-replaced wallet addresses can be monitored for outgoing cryptocurrency transactions
Potential download of extension code or updates from attacker infrastructure (if observed in network traffic)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of PyPI packages containing obfuscated code with non-Latin characters in identifiers. Detect creation or modification of %AppData%\Extension and browser shortcut files containing the --load-extension argument. Scan for browser extensions that monitor clipboard contents and use regular expressions to match cryptocurrency wallet addresses. Alert if clipboard contents are replaced with known attacker-controlled wallet addresses. Monitor for unexpected modifications to browser shortcut files and the presence of suspicious extension directories.
